sections.title: The Failure of Traditional Geometry
lecture_lines: Traditional geometry defines points, lines, and planes.
Some shapes are too complex for these dimensions.
Rough shapes like coastlines defy standard measurement.
animations: Display title: #FFFFFF 'The Failure of Traditional Geometry'.
Display #00FF00 square area one and #0000FF cube volume one, showing zoom on curve.

sections.title: Self-Similarity and Scaling
lecture_lines: Self-similar shapes look identical when you zoom in.
Scaling laws describe these recurring, detailed patterns.
We define scaling as N equals S to D.
animations: Show #FFFF00 shape, zooming into self-similar part.
Animate repeating #FF00FF pattern at smaller scales using N equals S to D.

sections.title: Deriving the Fractal Dimension
lecture_lines: Solve for dimension using logarithms of N and S.
The formula is D equals log N over log S.
For Koch snowflakes, dimension is one point two six.
Higher dimensions mean more space-filling complexity.
This fractional value measures a shape's roughness.
animations: Animate variables #00FFFF N and #FFFF00 s changing.
Highlight formula for Koch snowflake: #FF00FF D = 1.26.

sections.title: Fractals in Nature and Engineering
lecture_lines: Nature uses fractals to maximize surface area.
Lungs and antennas utilize this principle efficiently.
High fractal dimension allows compact, complex functions.
animations: Display title: #FFFFFF 'Fractals in Nature and Engineering'.
Show coastline #00FF00 example and tree branch #FF8000 growth.
Show antenna #FF00FF shape simulation, highlighting compactness.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
lecture_lines: Look for self-similarity in everyday patterns.
Simple recursive rules create infinite, natural detail.
